dimensions.reasons: The submitted scene visibly contains the core snowboarding setup: a dark-clothed helmeted rider, teal snowboard with blue bindings, groomed white slope, rocky/snowy embankment, and a trailing white spray. However, the Group C animation frames and Group B final frames depict a toy-like rear-facing rider sliding across a highly stylized low-poly slope rather than the close, realistic, dynamically framed carving sequence in the reference.
issues: Camera framing and viewpoint differ substantially: the reference tightly follows the rider from changing front/side/rear angles, while Group C stays largely behind the rider.
The reference's detailed rocky embankment is replaced with a continuous row of oversized faceted snow mounds and sparse geometric boulders.
The reference progresses to a sharply raised board with diffuse powder, whereas the submitted sequence mostly shows a nearly horizontal board and a blob-like trailing effect.
Terrain grooves are overly uniform blue-gray parallel lines rather than varied packed-snow tracks, seams, and scraped patches.

dimensions.reasons: The rider's feet are visibly placed at the blue bindings, but the structural continuity of the figure is poor. In Group B frame_0027 and Group C frames 0007-0016, the right forearm/hand pieces visibly separate and float away from the arm; similar gaps appear at other limb joints. The snowboard also repeatedly casts a separated shadow with a clear gap beneath it rather than credibly edge-contacting the snow.
issues: Both arms are assembled from disconnected oval pieces, with especially large floating gaps at the right wrist/hand.
Several knee, hip, and boot joints read as detached rather than as a connected rider rig.
The board is visibly unsupported above the snow in multiple Group C frames, including frames 0006-0011.
The powder trail is partly floating as isolated blobs and does not appear to be emitted continuously from a board edge or tail.

dimensions.reasons: The intended major silhouettes remain recognizable: black helmet/head, dark jacket and pants, bright blue bindings, and a long dark teal snowboard are clear in Group B frame_0001 and Group C frame_0001. The color palette broadly follows the reference's black outerwear, blue bindings, and dark green board.
issues: The rider reads as a segmented mannequin made of smooth capsules and spheres rather than a person in padded snow gear.
The reference's recognizable goggles with reflective purple/amber lens and strap are reduced to an indistinct dark-blue face-covering form.
There is little visual distinction between jacket, gloves, boots, and the highly glossy black limb pieces.
The faceted embankment rocks and snow pieces do not resemble the irregular natural rock-and-snow surfaces in the reference.

dimensions.reasons: The submitted images are cleanly rendered and maintain a coherent cold outdoor palette, but the Group B and Group C frames look like a simplified low-poly previs rather than the believable snowboarding footage requested. Plastic-like rider materials, disconnected anatomy, uniformly lined snow, and puffball spray substantially reduce realism.
issues: The rider is visibly constructed from primitive forms with unconvincing anatomy and disconnected joints.
Snow surfaces are smooth/faceted and lack the granular packed-snow detail of the reference.
The powder is a sequence of opaque rounded blobs instead of a diffuse, turbulent snow plume.
Motion-blur/softness in several action views makes small rider and spray details less legible.

dimensions.reasons: The basic spatial arrangement is present: the rider is on the sloped snowfield with a rocky, snow-covered ridge behind. This is clear in Group B frame_0001 and the wide Group A views. However, the submitted camera places the rider predominantly rear-on and centered, while the reference uses a close tracking perspective with the rider and board diagonally crossing the frame through distinct turn states.
issues: The rider orientation and camera relationship do not reproduce the close front/side-to-rear reference progression.
The board remains broadly horizontal across the image rather than rotating strongly into the raised final pose.
The embankment is arranged as a long, regular border of mounds rather than the irregular rocky slope immediately behind the rider.
Group A wide_front and wide_back reveal a much more open, staged slope than the compact, rider-focused reference composition.

dimensions.reasons: The board is approximately human snowboard length relative to the rider, and the two blue bindings are spaced plausibly across it. The snowfield also reads as a broad slope in the Group A wide views.
issues: The rider's bulbous torso, limbs, hands, and boots are disproportionately large and toy-like compared with a human snowboarder.
The blue bindings are oversized, simple upright blocks rather than binding/boot assemblies.
Several background rocks and white mound segments look oversized and repetitive relative to the rider and slope.

dimensions.reasons: The snow receives soft illumination, the helmet has a readable glossy highlight, and the rider/board cast shadows. Group C frame_0001 therefore has basic material and lighting separation. Nevertheless, the reference has crisp low-angle sunlight with a long, prominent rider shadow and detailed fabric, snow, rock, and board material variation that are not matched.
issues: Lighting is comparatively diffuse and low-contrast, without the strong directional sunlight and long shadow seen in the reference.
Helmet and limb materials are too uniformly glossy/plastic.
The snow is mostly flat white with blue line markings instead of textured compacted snow.
Rock surfaces are dark low-poly facets with detached-looking white caps rather than integrated snow-covered stone.

dimensions.reasons: All large requested components are visibly represented: one helmeted black-clad rider, a snowboard, blue binding-like elements, a snowy slope with tracks, a rocky/snowy backdrop, and a white trailing spray. The Group C sequence also shows changing rider lean and a spray/trail growing behind the board.
issues: Detailed goggles, realistic boot/binding structure, jacket/hood construction, and snow accumulated on the board are missing or too indistinct.
The powder spray exists but does not convincingly reproduce the reference's diffuse snow cloud around the lifted board.
The visible motion does not fully include the reference's strong final board lift and edge-driven turn geometry.
The modeled terrain and embankment lack the reference's varied natural snow and exposed-rock detail.

criteria.criterion: A continuous outdoor snow slope functions as the riding surface.
criteria.evidence: Wide views show the rider positioned over a single expansive white ground plane that recedes uphill and is visibly angled, with grooves continuing across the riding area.

criteria.criterion: One articulated human snowboarder is recognizable as the principal moving subject.
criteria.evidence: The animation frames consistently show one humanoid rider with a head, torso, two arms, two legs, and a crouched balance pose as the sole action subject.

criteria.criterion: The rider stands on a recognizable elongated snowboard.
criteria.evidence: A long, rounded-end teal snowboard is clearly visible beneath the rider in the exported frames, with the rider's boots positioned over it.

criteria.criterion: The wider framing phases include a rough, partially snow-covered rocky bank beyond the riding surface.
criteria.evidence: The wider and action views place an elevated irregular ridge behind the riding surface, with numerous exposed angular dark rock forms and separate white snow-cap patches.

criteria.criterion: The rider reproduces the reference's black helmet and jacket with very dark navy or near-black snow pants.
criteria.evidence: The rider has a black rounded helmet and black torso/jacket form, while the leg and pant pieces consistently render as very dark navy.

criteria.criterion: The snowboard is dark green-black and has two bindings with vivid blue accents.
criteria.evidence: Close animation frames clearly show a dark teal-green board with two separate saturated bright-blue upright binding pieces.

criteria.criterion: The snow surface shows granular variation, shallow ridges, and crossing track marks.
criteria.evidence: The riding surface has many thin blue-gray linear grooves and a few curved marks, but it reads primarily as a smooth white plane rather than a clearly granular snow surface with visibly modeled shallow ridges.

criteria.criterion: The major surfaces reproduce the reference's broad snow, winter-fabric, solid-board, and powder material response.
criteria.evidence: The rider is visibly built from glossy/matte separated oval primitives, the snow is faceted low-poly geometry, and the plume is a chain of solid white blobs rather than convincing winter fabric and airborne powder material responses.

criteria.criterion: Feet, bindings, board, and slope maintain physically plausible attachment and contact.
criteria.evidence: Although the feet remain over the blue bindings, multiple sequence frames show a pronounced illuminated gap and shadow under the nearly level board, most clearly during frames 0006 through 0011.

criteria.criterion: The delivered project provides an editable rig that drives the snowboarder.
Continuous edge transitions drive linked curved turns with timing comparable to the reference.
criteria.evidence: The sampled sequence shows broad leaning and an upright reset, but the board remains visually close to a flat lateral orientation and the camera holds the rider centered, so linked curved path redirection and clear continuous edge-roll transitions are not unambiguously visible.

criteria.criterion: Body articulation communicates believable weight transfer during the turns.
criteria.evidence: The torso leans in parts of the sequence, but the arms and mitten ends are visibly separated by gaps and float away from their limb segments; the resulting pose changes do not clearly communicate coherent, connected weight transfer.

criteria.criterion: Loaded carving produces a visible displaced powder plume from the snowboard's tail.
criteria.evidence: A white puffy spray begins behind the left/trailing end of the board during the later leaning phase and grows into a longer trailing mass in the ordered animation frames.

criteria.criterion: The animation follows the reference's ordered posture, edge-transition, and powder progression.
criteria.evidence: The sequence includes an early upright pose, later leaning, and a growing white trail, but the late board state is visibly floating/near-flat rather than clearly edge-engaged, so the required finished carve progression is not convincingly established.

criteria.criterion: The camera reproduces the reference's readable rider scale, viewing angle, slope coverage, and lateral tracking.
criteria.evidence: In the authored animation frames the rider remains large and readable while the snowy slope and embankment remain in view; the background shifts laterally while the rider is maintained near center frame.

criteria.criterion: Bright directional daylight creates strong snow highlights and distinct cast shadows.
criteria.evidence: The scene is brightly lit and the helmet has a highlight, but rider and board shadows are soft, short, and weak beneath the board rather than the distinct long directional cast shadows visible in the reference.

criteria.criterion: The output video satisfies the requested container, codec, dimensions, frame rate, and approximate duration.
A usable editable Blender project containing the reconstructed scene and animation setup is delivered.
The rider has the reference-visible rounded helmet and eye-covering ski goggles.
criteria.evidence: The head has a rounded black dome, but the dark blue lower head form reads as a full face covering/visor-like blob with no distinct goggle lens shape or visible strap.

notes: The core subject is clearly recognizable as a snowboarder on a snowy slope with a board, bindings, rocks, and spray. The result is nevertheless a loose stylized previs rather than a faithful reconstruction: the camera/action progression, raised-board finish, realistic snow behavior, terrain detail, directional lighting, and connected rider anatomy all differ markedly from the reference.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
